corrections.why: The Register gives a range for the build year rather than one year; 1933 is only the start of that range.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says between 1933 and 1937. A Tumblr post says 1932 by the CCC and names no source for that date, so the story flags it as unsourced. The city's about 92 years points to roughly 1934, so the story follows the Register range.
Register gives 2,039 ft (621 m), matching the record's 621.5 m. The tnlandforms inventory gives 2021 feet for the same site; the record keeps the Register figure.

Register lists the State of Tennessee and notes several agencies deny ownership. Forest Lookouts names the Tennessee Division of Forestry. The wildlife agency page covers the surrounding Roosevelt Mountain WMA. The story reports the disagreement without choosing one.

sources.title: Post by moosenotgoose on the Rockwood Fire Tower

notes_for_editor: Build date conflicts across sources: Register range 1933 to 1937, an unsourced Tumblr post at 1932, and the city's 92 years. The city of Rockwood has an interest in getting the Star donated and its structural-soundness claim is the city's own. Only the Register and the city give a history; no staffing, fire or primary state record was found. The tnlandforms figure of 2021 feet differs from the Register's 2,039 ft, and its column labels were not confirmed. Access is set to restricted because the tower is fenced and the wildlife agency says not to climb it. The story's wildlife-area sentence follows the TWRA page, which describes the Roosevelt Mountain WMA rather than the mountain itself. No photos added. Not verified: whether the state has transferred the Star or started the planned restoration.
